runtime_gate.reason: Existing canonical F-host shared-runner heartbeat remains stale and height_difference_2 guarded operator recovery remains unexecuted.

score_basis: Non-statistical internal evidence-quality score based on adopted London policy, current 2026 Building Regulations guidance and explicit separation of strategic targets, scheme calculations and future policy evidence.

sources.label: London Plan 2021 Policy G5 Urban greening
sources.fact: Adopted policy requires major development to include urban greening; interim UGF targets are 0.4 for predominantly residential and 0.3 for predominantly commercial development excluding B2/B8.

sources.label: Urban Greening Factor guidance
sources.fact: Adopted London Plan Guidance dated 2 February 2023; provides a UGF calculator and application framework.

sources.label: London Plan 2021 Policy SI2
sources.fact: Major development should be net zero-carbon, follow the be lean/be clean/be green/be seen hierarchy, and demonstrate the target through a detailed energy strategy.

sources.label: London Plan SI2 on-site reduction
sources.fact: Adopted policy states a minimum 35% on-site reduction beyond Building Regulations for major development, with specified energy-efficiency components.

sources.label: Whole Life-Cycle Carbon Assessments guidance
sources.fact: Formally adopted GLA guidance explains WLC assessment and post-construction reporting; RICS second-edition methodology may additionally be provided while GLA guidance remains the reporting basis for referable schemes.

sources.label: Approved Document L 2026
sources.fact: Published 24 March 2026 for England; supports Part L and notes earlier versions continue for buildings subject to previous regulatory standards.

sources.label: Approved Document O overheating FAQ
sources.fact: Part O sets overheating standards for new residential buildings and does not generally apply to later extensions or conservatories added after construction.

sources.label: London Plan evidence - UGF implementation and target review
sources.fact: The next-London-Plan evidence page lists an Urban Greening Factor implementation and target review dated July 2026.

sources.label: London Plan evidence - operational energy policies
sources.fact: The evidence base lists operational-energy policy evidence dated July 2026; it is evidence for future policy development, not adopted parcel requirements.

sources.label: London Plan evidence - whole life carbon future policy
sources.fact: July 2026 whole-life-carbon evidence is listed for the next London Plan and remains distinct from the adopted 2021 policy/guidance framework.

sources.label: London Green Infrastructure Framework
sources.fact: The evidence page lists the London Green Infrastructure Framework dated May 2026 as supporting evidence.

sources.label: London Plan G5 heat/SuDS rationale
sources.fact: Urban greening measures can address urban heat island effects and sustainable drainage, but those benefits require scheme-specific design evidence.

examples.result: UGF 0.4/0.3 values retained as adopted interim design targets, not parcel feasibility scores.
B2/B8 exclusion from the 0.3 commercial interim UGF target retained; no generic target backfill.
SI2 35% on-site reduction is a major-development policy test, not evidence that an unverified parcel can achieve it.
Approved Document L 2026 and earlier transitional standards are version-gated; no silent replacement across regulatory vintages.
Part O is treated as a new-residential overheating requirement, not a generic constraint for every building alteration.
July 2026 next-plan UGF/energy/WLC evidence is tagged FUTURE_POLICY_EVIDENCE and not substituted for adopted policy.
WLC guidance is reporting/assessment evidence; no embodied-carbon value is invented without a scheme assessment.
Urban heat/SuDS benefit statements do not create parcel-level quantitative benefits without design and geometry evidence.
